title: Settlement Basis: Value Carried onto a Fresh Travel Credit Voucher on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
**What is settled, and in what order.** The value standing under Air Ticket Fare Brands is the largest lapsed travel credit standing on the booking. The value carried onto the fresh travel credit voucher is that value standing once every share and every uplift that bears on it has been taken, with anything taken off in dollars, the reissue fee charged on the booking above all, taken off last of all, after every share and every uplift, and it is never below zero. The value standing is the figure settled first, and the value carried follows from it in that order, each share and each uplift acting in turn on the figure the one before it gives, so that the figure runs on from one step to the next and is never reached by measuring them separately against the value standing and netting the results together.

**How several adjustments of one kind act on one figure.** Where more than one share is taken on the same figure, the shares act one after another, each on the figure the one before it gives, and are never combined into a single rate; where more than one uplift is added to the same figure, the uplifts are combined into a single uplift and the figure is increased once by that total.

**The quantities read.** The largest lapsed travel credit standing on the booking is the greatest value among the lapsed travel credit issue lines posted to that booking. The reissue fee charged on the booking is the reissue fee standing as a charged line on it, taken as the total of the credit reissue fee lines standing charged to the booking. The reissue fee is met once, out of the value being carried forward, and is never taken a second time out of the vouchers it was charged for. The travel credit validity term of the fare brand that produced the lapsed voucher governs how long the fresh voucher runs.

**Whether anything is owed at all.** The travel credit vouchers standing on the booking are taken as one set, and the set stands lapsed when the voucher most recently issued on it has lapsed. Where that voucher has not lapsed, the set is still redeemable as it stands and nothing is owed under this rule.

**How the fresh voucher is filed.** It is filed against the issue line of the largest lapsed voucher standing on the booking and carries the traveller position of that line, so it stands in the name of the traveller at that position. It runs for the same validity term as the voucher it replaces, counted from the day it is reissued. The traveller carries the value forward themselves, because it is their own once-only right of reissue that is spent.

**Rounding.** The value carried is rounded to two decimal places at the end of the determination and at no intermediate step.

**The determination, on hypothetical figures.** Every figure and every rate in what follows is hypothetical, chosen only to show the whole chain being carried, and no rate below is a published one. Take a booking whose value standing settles at 640.00 US dollars, and follow the whole chain from that settled figure. Suppose a share of 0.62 bears on it: 640.00 taken at 0.62 gives 396.80. Suppose an uplift of 0.42 then bears on the figure that share gave: 396.80 increased by 0.42 gives 563.456. Each step is worked on the figure the step before it gave, and no step is worked on the 640.00 the stage settled at. Against a reissue fee charged on that booking of 75.00 US dollars, that fee comes off last of all, after every share and every uplift, leaving 488.456; the figure is above zero, so the rule that it is never below zero leaves it as it stands, and rounded to two decimal places at the end the value carried is 488.46 US dollars. Take instead a booking whose value standing settles at 60.00 US dollars: carried through the same hypothetical share of 0.62 it gives 37.20, and through the same hypothetical uplift of 0.42 it gives 52.824. Against a reissue fee charged of 75.00 US dollars, taking the fee off last would carry the figure below zero, so the value carried is 0.00 US dollars. On the same hypothetical ground, were shares of 0.64 and then 0.72 taken on a figure of 400.00 US dollars, the first would give 256.00 and the second would act on that 256.00, giving 184.32; were uplifts of 0.13 and 0.24 added to a figure of 400.00 US dollars, they would be combined into a single uplift of 0.37 and that figure increased once by that total, giving 548.00.
